newsitem.title: USA: Wolfensohn says Chinese economy doing well.
newsitem.headline: Wolfensohn says Chinese economy doing well.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn said on Friday the Chinese economy was growing well, but the international lending organisation still had an important role to play there.
Speaking at a press conference at the World Bank's spring meeting, Wolfensohn said "China is moving along pretty damn well at the moment."
But the World Bank chief added that huge distortions still existed in the Chinese economy which the bank could tackle in an effort to make the country more attractive to foreign investment.
"We have plenty of business in China," Wolfensohn said. "We can bring expertise in areas like poverty alleviation."
He said that although China already pulls in a disproportionate share of global capital, the bank would continue to look for ways to make the country still more attractive to private investors.

The World Bank's sister organisation, the International Monetary Fund, said earlier this week that it expected China's economy to grow 9.5 percent in 1997, down slightly from 9.7 percent seen for 1996.
The IMF forecast that inflation there would remain steady at six percent.
